draft.title: I made a Bitcoin/gold scenario calculator to explain a common percentage mistake
draft.body:
If Bitcoin rises 10% and gold rises 5%, how much does Bitcoin's value in gold change? The answer is about 4.76%, because the ratio changes by 1.10 / 1.05 - 1. Subtracting the two percentages only approximates the result.

I'm building BTC2G with AI coding assistance to make comparisons like this easier to inspect. It combines historical BTC/gold ratios, a reference calculator, and a what-if simulator. The interface uses JavaScript and static HTML, including crawlable pages in 19 languages. Sources and market dates are shown.

You can change the two hypothetical price moves at https://btc2g.com/scenario.html without creating an account. The inputs describe an arithmetic scenario; they do not predict returns. The history uses published BTC-USD and gold-futures reference data rather than an executable trade quote.

I'd appreciate feedback on whether the formula and inputs are understandable on a phone. What explanation would help someone avoid mixing up dollar returns with changes in the BTC/gold ratio?
